167. It must not be thought that forms generate others like themselves within matter; for generating is a property of bodies. Rather, it is the right and duty of the **form** to move its organs harmoniously, and through them to prepare the seminal matter for generation. The form encloses within that matter a ray of light, or a secret spark of life, as if it were a treasure. It imprints its own specific character upon that vivifying spirit hidden in the seed, which, in the work of generation—driven by a pulsating heat and at a fixed time—unfolds itself into a **Soul** <note>original: "Animam." In this philosophical context, the soul is the life-force or organizing principle of any living thing, whether plant or animal.</note>, whether vegetable or animal. Thus, that which had been a secret and formal spirit within the seed becomes the **Form** <note>The active, defining essence of a being.</note> within the compound. <summary>This page describes how the "form" or organizing principle of a being guides reproduction by imprinting a "spark of life" upon the seed. This process allows species to achieve a version of immortality by passing their divine blueprint from one generation to the next.</summary>
<keywords>Generation, Form, Seminal Matter, Soul, Vivifying Spirit, Natural Philosophy, Immortality of Species</keywords>
